title: MACP Agent Bootstrap Payload
description: Canonical schema for the bootstrap payload written to MACP_BOOTSTRAP_FILE before an agent process is spawned. Consumed by the agent at startup to learn its runId, sessionId, runtime address + Bearer token, and — for the initiator agent only — the SessionStart payload and the first kickoff envelope template. See direct-agent-auth architecture (§Invariants).

sessionId.description: Pre-allocated session identifier the initiator will bind at SessionStart. Satisfies runtime validation: UUID v4/v7 or base64url 22+ chars.

participantId.description: The agent's sender id. Must match the authenticated identity on the runtime (RFC-MACP-0004 §4).

agentId.description: Agent catalog reference (e.g. 'fraud-agent'). May equal participantId.

address.description: gRPC endpoint of the MACP runtime, e.g. '127.0.0.1:50051' or 'runtime.internal:50051'.

bearerToken.description: This agent's own Bearer token. Must match an identity in the runtime's MACP_AUTH_TOKENS_JSON whose 'sender' equals participant.participantId.

tls.description: If true, use TLS for the gRPC channel. Default true in production: RFC-MACP-0004 Section 2 (Transport Security) requires encrypted transport, and for gRPC over HTTP/2 requires TLS 1.2 or higher.

allowInsecure.description: Dev-only escape hatch permitting a plaintext channel. Must be false in production. NON-NORMATIVE note: within this bootstrap document the two fields are separate inputs -- tls states whether TLS is wanted, allowInsecure whether plaintext is tolerated -- but how an SDK combines them (whether allowInsecure alone may select plaintext, or only permit it) is NOT settled here. The two SDKs currently differ, and that default is each SDK's connection-security behavior, so it is theirs to reconcile; see the cross-SDK transport issue.

controlPlaneBaseUrl.description: HTTP URL for read-only observability: GET /runs/:id, /runs/:id/events. Not used for envelope emission (agents emit via gRPC).

controlPlaneApiKey.description: Optional API key for the control-plane HTTP reads above.

initiator.description: Populated ONLY on the initiator agent's bootstrap. The initiator calls MacpClient.send(SessionStart) with sessionStart, awaits ack, then emits kickoff (when present) as its first mode-scoped envelope.

contextId.description: Globally-unique context reference (e.g. ctx:sha256:<hex>, a URI, or any opaque string). The runtime preserves it but MUST NOT interpret it. Embedded as SessionStartPayload.context_id, a proto string, so this is a plain JSON string and is NOT base64-encoded.

extensions.description: Generic extension blocks keyed by protocol identifier. Values are base64-encoded protocol-specific bytes. Embedded as SessionStartPayload.extensions, a map<string, bytes>; per RFC-MACP-0001 Section 10.3 protobuf bytes fields MUST be represented as base64-encoded strings in JSON. A caller wanting to carry structured data base64-encodes its own serialization, so the inner format is the caller's declared choice rather than the SDK's guess. Note contentEncoding is an annotation in JSON Schema 2020-12, not an assertion: this schema declares the encoding, it does not validate it.

additionalProperties.description: Protobuf bytes mapped to base64 string in JSON.

maxSuspendMs.description: Embedded as SessionStartPayload.max_suspend_ms. Upper bound on cumulative time the session may spend SUSPENDED (RFC-MACP-0001 Section 7.5).

kickoff.description: Optional first mode-scoped envelope the initiator emits immediately after SessionStart is accepted (e.g., a Proposal for decision mode, a TaskRequest for task mode). May be absent for modes where the initiator opens the session but any participant may speak first.

payload.description: Pre-encoded payload bytes (base64 / proto-encoded) ready to place in Envelope.payload.

cancelCallback.description: Local HTTP endpoint the agent exposes so the control-plane's UI-cancel path (direct-agent-auth Option A) can ask the initiator to call CancelSession on the runtime with its own identity (RFC-MACP-0001 §7.2).

session.description: Non-authoritative session-context hints. Used by agent frameworks for display/setup only.

execution.description: Scenario metadata surfaced to the agent for framework setup (scenarioRef, modeName, tags, requester). Free-form; opaque to the runtime.

agent.description: Framework-specific bootstrap data (manifest, framework name, framework config).
